findings.correction: Remove the generic figure value assigned to every source. Populate a source-specific figure only after verifying it; otherwise cite the named method section, abstract, or result location. Do not present a generic methods phrase as an actual figure citation.

The existing Gerhardt, Hellström, and Suchting studies support VEGF guidance and tip–stalk/branch regulation, not the displayed sprout-lumen-extension stage. A primary lumenogenesis study can support general vascular lumen formation, but the cited aortic context should be made explicit and must not be described as direct evidence for capillary-sprout lumen extension.

primary_release_evidence.claim_scope: A generic chemical-synapse workflow can state that presynaptic calcium entry is coupled to vesicular transmitter release, while avoiding claims about a particular transmitter, receptor subtype, or universal clearance route.

sources.citation: Dodge FA Jr, Rahamimoff R. Co-operative action of calcium ions in transmitter release at the neuromuscular junction. J Physiol. 1967;193(2):419–432.
sources.support_location: Intracellular electrophysiology at frog neuromuscular junction; end-plate potentials used as a measure of released quanta under varied calcium conditions.

sources.citation: Geppert M et al. Synaptotagmin I: a major Ca2+ sensor for transmitter release at a central synapse. Cell. 1994;79(4):717–727.
sources.support_location: Mutant-mouse and cultured hippocampal-neuron results support calcium-triggered synchronous transmitter release.

primary_release_evidence.limitation: These sources support calcium-dependent release, not every stage or receptor/clearance mechanism in the generic template. A single sequence diagram should keep those downstream details generic or cite additional primary studies for the specific claim.
